question: Jitesh sold an article at a loss of 11%. If he had bought the item at 5% less and had sold it for ₹739 more, then he would have gained 20%. Find the cost price (in ₹) of the article.
solution:
**Given:**

Loss = 11%

New cost price = Original cost price - 5%

New selling price = Original selling price + ₹739

Profit in new scenario = 20%

**Formula used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) × (1 ± Profit/Loss%)

Profit% = (Profit)/(CP) times 100

Loss% = (Loss)/(CP) times 100

**Calculations:**

Let the original cost price be ₹x.

Original selling price = x × (1 - 11/100) = x × (89/100)

New cost price = x × (95/100)

New selling price = x × (89/100) + ₹739

From the new scenario:

New selling price = New cost price × (1 + 20/100)

⇒ x × (89/100) + ₹739 = x × (95/100) × (120/100)

⇒ x × (89/100) + ₹739 = x × (114/100)

⇒ ₹739 = x × (114/100) - x × (89/100)

⇒ ₹739 = x × [(114 - 89)/100]

⇒ ₹739 = x × (25/100)

⇒ x = ₹739 × (100/25)

⇒ x = ₹2956

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**
